label: Review of Group Theory
notes: This appendix is the algebra toolkit for the fundamental group and covering spaces. We treat the symmetry group of a triangle as a microscope: small enough to enumerate, rich enough to show noncommutativity, normal subgroups, quotients, and actions. If a construction fails here, it is unsafe in topology.

label: The Group Axioms
notes: A group is a set with an associative product, an identity, and inverses for every element. Associativity is what lets us drop parentheses when concatenating loops or composing covering transformations. We verify all four axioms by enumeration on the six triangle symmetries, the running finite model.

label: Abelian Groups and Cayley Graphs
notes: Abelian means the product commutes. The Cayley graph draws one colored arrow per generator, so generation and commutativity become visible. If the generator arrows fail to close into squares at every node, the group is nonabelian, exactly the case for the triangle symmetries where rs differs from sr.

label: Subgroups, Cosets, Lagrange
notes: A subgroup is a subset closed under product and inverse. Left cosets partition the whole group into blocks all the same size as the subgroup. Counting blocks gives Lagrange's theorem: the order of a subgroup divides the order of the group, a constant background fact in covering theory.

label: Homomorphisms and Isomorphisms
notes: A homomorphism preserves the product; an isomorphism is a bijective one. The kernel collects everything sent to the identity, recording what the map forgets, while the image is what it reaches. Induced maps on fundamental groups are homomorphisms, so kernel and image are the invariants we will track.

label: Normal Subgroups and Quotients
notes: A subgroup is normal when conjugation keeps it set-wise fixed. Normality is exactly the condition making coset multiplication independent of representatives, so the quotient becomes a genuine group. Kernels are always normal, which is why every homomorphism manufactures a quotient on its domain side.

label: First Isomorphism Theorem
notes: Every homomorphism factors as a surjection onto a quotient by its kernel, followed by an isomorphism onto its image. The sign map on triangle symmetries collapses six elements to two cosets, then identifies that quotient with the two signs, a clean finite instance of the theorem.

label: Cyclic Groups Z and Z mod n
notes: A cyclic group is generated by one element: the integers under addition or the residues modulo n. They are the simplest infinite and finite groups and appear as fundamental groups of the circle and lens spaces. Every subgroup of a cyclic group is again cyclic.

label: Direct Products
notes: The direct product multiplies coordinates independently, so its order is the product of factor orders. When the factor orders are coprime the product is itself cyclic; here the two and three element cyclic groups combine into the six element cyclic group by the Chinese remainder correspondence.

label: Group Actions
notes: An action lets group elements move points of a set: the identity fixes everything and products act in sequence. The orbit of a point is what it reaches; the stabilizer is the subgroup fixing it. Actions are the bridge from algebra to quotient spaces and covering transformations.

label: Orbit-Stabilizer
notes: The orbit-stabilizer relation says the group size equals orbit size times stabilizer size, because the stabilizer cosets index the orbit. For the triangle acting on its three vertices, six symmetries split into three fibers of two, the finite preview of degree counts for covering maps.

label: Recap and Bridge to Topology
notes: We assembled axioms, cosets and Lagrange, homomorphisms with kernels, normal subgroups and quotients, the first isomorphism theorem, cyclic groups and products, and actions with orbit-stabilizer. These are exactly the moves used to compute fundamental groups and to organize covering spaces in the chapters ahead.
